question: Among four colleagues, the total monthly savings is ₹40,000. X and Y together save as much as Z and W. X saves ₹2,000 more than Z. W saves three times as much as Z. Who saves the least amount?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Z.

GIVEN

• X + Y + Z + W = 40,000. X + Y = Z + W. X = Z + 2,000. W = 3Z.

SOLUTION

• Since X + Y = Z + W and the total is 40,000, Z + W = 20,000 and X + Y = 20,000.

• W = 3Z, so Z + 3Z = 20,000, 4Z = 20,000 and Z = 5,000. Then W = 15,000.

• X = Z + 2,000 = 7,000. Y = 20,000 − 7,000 = 13,000.

• Savings: X = ₹7,000, Y = ₹13,000, Z = ₹5,000, W = ₹15,000. The least is Z.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Two equal halves of ₹20,000 each; W is three times Z, so Z is one-fourth of its half: 20,000 ÷ 4 = 5,000, which is lower than X's 7,000.

NOTE

• Option 1 (X) is wrong: X saves ₹7,000, which is more than Z. Option 2 (Y) is wrong: Y saves ₹13,000. Option 4 (W) is wrong: W saves ₹15,000, the largest amount.

question: A chef divides a large chocolate bar into two equal halves. One half is kept aside, and the other half is broken into 8 smaller, equal square pieces. Each square piece weighs 15 grams. What is the total weight of the original chocolate bar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 240 grams.

GIVEN

• The bar is divided into 2 equal halves. One half = 8 pieces of 15 grams each.

SOLUTION

• Weight of one half = 8 × 15 = 120 grams

• The two halves are equal, so the whole bar = 2 × 120 = 240 grams

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Find one half first, then double it: (8 × 15) × 2 = 240.

NOTE

• Option 1 (280 grams) is wrong: each half would be 140 g, which is not 8 × 15. Option 2 (220 grams) is wrong: each half would be 110 g. Option 4 (260 grams) is wrong: each half would be 130 g.

question: In the following question, a matrix of numbers is given. These numbers follow a certain pattern either row-wise or column-wise. Identify this pattern and choose the missing number accordingly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 36.

GIVEN

• Matrix: Row 1: 25, 60, 40; Row 2: 6, 40, 16; Row 3: 14, ?, 23

SOLUTION

• In each row, middle number = 4 × (third number − first number).

• Row 1: 4 × (40 − 25) = 4 × 15 = 60 ✓. Row 2: 4 × (16 − 6) = 4 × 10 = 40 ✓.

• Row 3: 4 × (23 − 14) = 4 × 9 = 36

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Use two complete rows to test a rule; once a rule such as 4 × (difference of the end numbers) fits both, apply it to the incomplete row.

NOTE

• Option 1 (32), Option 2 (44) and Option 4 (40) are wrong: they are not equal to 4 × (23 − 14) = 36, so they break the pattern of the first two rows.

question: In the following question, a matrix of numbers is given. These numbers follow a certain pattern either row-wise or column-wise. Identify this pattern and choose the missing number accordingly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 24.

GIVEN

• Matrix: Row 1: 15, 42, ?; Row 2: 6, 18, 24; Row 3: 27, 78, 72

SOLUTION

• Look at each column: the third number = first number + 2 × second number.

• Column 1: 15 + 2 × 6 = 27 ✓. Column 2: 42 + 2 × 18 = 78 ✓.

• Column 3: ? + 2 × 24 = 72, so ? = 72 − 48 = 24

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• When the row-wise rule does not fit, test column-wise rules: use the two complete columns to find that row 3 = row 1 + 2 × row 2.

NOTE

• Option 1 (58), Option 2 (30) and Option 4 (62) are wrong: with them, the column rule gives 58 + 48 = 106, 30 + 48 = 78 and 62 + 48 = 110, none of which equals 72.

question:
Select the number that will come next in the following series.

5, 10, 20, 40, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 80.

GIVEN

• Series: 5, 10, 20, 40, ?

SOLUTION

• Each term is double the previous term: 5 × 2 = 10, 10 × 2 = 20, 20 × 2 = 40.

• Next term: 40 × 2 = 80

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Divide each term by the one before it; if the ratio is the same (2), multiply the last term by that ratio.

question:

729, 243, 81, 27, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 9.

GIVEN

• Series: 729, 243, 81, 27, ?

SOLUTION

• Each term is one-third of the previous term: 729 ÷ 3 = 243, 243 ÷ 3 = 81, 81 ÷ 3 = 27.

• Next term: 27 ÷ 3 = 9

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

• These are powers of 3: 729 = 3⁶, 243 = 3⁵, 81 = 3⁴, 27 = 3³, so the next is 3² = 9.

NOTE

• Option 1 (3) is wrong: it is 3¹, which skips 3². Option 3 (6) and Option 4 (12) are wrong: they are not powers of 3 and do not equal 27 ÷ 3.

question: A month has 30 days and its 1st day is Saturday. On which date will the fifth Sunday fall?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 30th.

GIVEN

• The month has 30 days. 1st = Saturday.

SOLUTION

• If the 1st is Saturday, the 2nd is Sunday.

• The Sundays are 2nd, 9th, 16th, 23rd and 30th.

• The fifth Sunday is on the 30th.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• The first Sunday = 2nd. Add 7 each time, or compute: 2 + 4 × 7 = 30.

NOTE

• Option 1 (23rd) is wrong: it is the fourth Sunday. Option 2 (29th) is wrong: it is a Saturday. Option 4 (31st) is wrong: the month has only 30 days.

question: In an ordinary year, which pair of months will have the same calendar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. January and October.

GIVEN

• An ordinary (non-leap) year has 365 days. We need two months that start on the same weekday and also have the same number of days.

SOLUTION

• January 1 to October 1 = 31 + 28 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 31 + 30 = 273 days = 39 weeks exactly, so both months begin on the same weekday. January and October both have 31 days, so their calendars are exactly the same.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Same-calendar pairs of months in an ordinary year: January–October, April–July (start on the same day), February–March–November (start on the same day), and September–December. Only the pair whose months also have the same number of days has the same calendar: January and October (31 and 31).

NOTE

• Option 2 (February and November) is wrong: the two months start on the same weekday, but February has 28 days and November has 30. Option 3 (April and July) is wrong: April has 30 days and July has 31. Option 4 (September and December) is wrong: September has 30 days and December has 31.

question: A faulty clock loses 10 minutes every hour. It was set correct at 12 noon. When the clock shows 3:00 PM, what is the actual time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 3:36 PM.

GIVEN

• The clock loses 10 minutes every hour: in 60 real minutes it shows only 50 minutes. Set right at 12:00 noon; now it shows 3:00 PM.

SOLUTION

• Time shown by the clock = 3 hours = 180 minutes.

• 50 clock minutes = 60 real minutes, so 180 clock minutes = 180 × 60 ÷ 50 = 216 real minutes = 3 hours 36 minutes.

• Actual time = 12:00 noon + 3 h 36 min = 3:36 PM

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Real time = clock time × 60/50 = clock time × 6/5. So 3 hours × 6/5 = 3.6 hours = 3 h 36 min.

NOTE

• Option 1 (3:24 PM) is wrong: it is 204 real minutes, in which the clock would show only 170 minutes. Option 2 (3:30 PM) is wrong: 210 real minutes correspond to 175 clock minutes. (The PDF shows this option as a wrong selection.) Option 4 (3:40 PM) is wrong: 220 real minutes correspond to about 183 clock minutes, not 180.

question: In a certain code language, 'doctor checks patient daily' is written as 'ja mo li su', 'nurse checks report carefully' is written as 'pe mo ra ki', 'patient gets medicine daily' is written as 'li fu ta su' and 'medicine and report' is written as 'ta ra ne'. What is the code for 'doctor'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ja.

GIVEN

• doctor checks patient daily = ja mo li su

• nurse checks report carefully = pe mo ra ki

• patient gets medicine daily = li fu ta su

• medicine and report = ta ra ne

SOLUTION

• "checks" is common to statements 1 and 2, and "mo" is common to the codes, so checks = mo.

• "patient" and "daily" are common to statements 1 and 3, and "li" and "su" are common to the codes, so {patient, daily} = {li, su}.

• In statement 1 the codes are ja, mo, li, su; mo = checks and li, su = patient, daily. The only code left is ja, which is the code for "doctor".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Find the common words and common codes between statements, remove them from the first statement, and what remains is the answer.

NOTE

• Option 1 (mo) is wrong: it is the code for "checks". Option 3 (li) is wrong: it is the code for "patient" or "daily". Option 4 (ta) is wrong: it is the code for "medicine" (common to statements 3 and 4).

question: If A = −, B = ÷, C = +, D = ×, find: 20 A 5 B 5 C 6 D 2 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 31.

GIVEN

• A = −, B = ÷, C = +, D = ×. Expression: 20 A 5 B 5 C 6 D 2.

SOLUTION

• Replace the letters with the signs: 20 − 5 ÷ 5 + 6 × 2

• Apply BODMAS (division and multiplication first): 5 ÷ 5 = 1 and 6 × 2 = 12

• 20 − 1 + 12 = 31

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Write the real symbols first, then do ÷ and × before + and −.

NOTE

• Option 1 (27), Option 2 (29) and Option 4 (33) are wrong: they do not come from 20 − 1 + 12. For example, working from left to right without BODMAS gives (20 − 5) ÷ 5 + 6 × 2 = 3 + 12 = 15 or similar values, which are also not the answer.

question: In a certain code language SUMMER is written as ‘VTLNDQ’ and WINTER is written as ‘ZHMUDQ’. How will SPRING be written in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. VOQJMF.

GIVEN

• SUMMER → VTLNDQ and WINTER → ZHMUDQ. Find the code for SPRING.

SOLUTION

• SUMMER → VTLNDQ: S + 3 = V, U − 1 = T, M − 1 = L, M + 1 = N, E − 1 = D, R − 1 = Q.

• WINTER → ZHMUDQ: W + 3 = Z, I − 1 = H, N − 1 = M, T + 1 = U, E − 1 = D, R − 1 = Q.

• The shifts by position are the same: +3, −1, −1, +1, −1, −1.

• SPRING: S + 3 = V, P − 1 = O, R − 1 = Q, I + 1 = J, N − 1 = M, G − 1 = F

• Code = VOQJMF

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Compare the two given words position by position to get the list of shifts, then apply the list to the new word.

NOTE

• Option 2 (VOJPFN), Option 3 (VOPJNF) and Option 4 (VQOMJF) are wrong: they have the same letters in a wrong order or with wrong shifts (the third letter must be Q, the fourth J, and the second O).

question: How many times do the hour and minute hands coincide between 10:00 and 3:00?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 4 times.

GIVEN

• Time interval: from 10:00 to 3:00 (5 hours).

SOLUTION

• The hands coincide once every 12/11 hours = 65 5/11 minutes. In 12 hours they coincide 11 times (at 12:00 only once).

• Coincidences after 12:00: 12:00, 1:05:27, 2:10:55, 3:16:22, ....

• Between 10:00 and 3:00 the hands coincide at about 10:54, 12:00, 1:05 and 2:10, which is 4 times. (The next coincidence, at 3:16, is after 3:00.)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• In every full hour interval the hands coincide once, except between 11 and 1 where they coincide only once at 12:00. For 10 to 3: 10–11 (1), 11–12 and 12–1 (together 1, at 12:00), 1–2 (1) and 2–3 (1) = 4.

NOTE

• Option 1 (3 times) is wrong: it misses one of the coincidences (10:54, 12:00, 1:05 or 2:10). Option 2 (5 times) is wrong: it counts the 12:00 hour twice or includes 3:16. Option 4 (6 times) is wrong: the hands coincide only once per hour at most. (The PDF shows this option as a wrong selection.)

question: A father was three times as old as his son 8 years ago. After 12 years, he will be twice as old as his son. What is the present age of the father?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 68 years.

GIVEN

• Let the father's present age = F and the son's present age = S. F − 8 = 3(S − 8) and F + 12 = 2(S + 12).

SOLUTION

• First equation: F = 3S − 24 + 8 = 3S − 16

• Second equation: F = 2S + 24 − 12 = 2S + 12

• Equate: 3S − 16 = 2S + 12, so S = 28 and F = 2 × 28 + 12 = 68 years

• Check: 8 years ago the father was 60 and the son was 20 (60 = 3 × 20 ✓). After 12 years the father will be 80 and the son 40 (80 = 2 × 40 ✓).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Test the options with the first condition: the father's age 8 years ago must be divisible by 3 (and give the son's age 8 years ago). 68 − 8 = 60 works.

NOTE

• Option 1 (36 years) is wrong: 36 − 8 = 28 is not divisible by 3. Option 2 (40 years) is wrong: 40 − 8 = 32 is not divisible by 3. Option 4 (66 years) is wrong: 66 − 8 = 58 is not divisible by 3.

question: The ratio of present ages of A and B is 3 : 4. After 8 years, A's age will be equal to B's age 4 years ago. What is B's present age?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 48 years.

GIVEN

• A : B = 3 : 4, so let A = 3x and B = 4x. A's age after 8 years = B's age 4 years ago.

SOLUTION

• 3x + 8 = 4x − 4

• x = 12

• B's present age = 4 × 12 = 48 years (and A = 36)

• Check: A after 8 years = 44; B 4 years ago = 44 ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• B's present age must be a multiple of 4. The gap between the two ages (8 + 4 = 12) equals 1 part (4x − 3x = x), so x = 12 and B = 4 × 12 = 48.

NOTE

• Option 1 (44 years) is wrong: x = 11 would give A after 8 years = 41 but B four years ago = 40. Option 2 (46 years) and Option 4 (50 years) are wrong: they are not multiples of 4, so the ratio 3 : 4 cannot hold.

question: A locker code was remembered as PQ91X, PQ92X, PR91X, and PQ81X. All four agreed on the first and last characters, and three agreed on each of the remaining positions. What is the correct code?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

question: Choose the option that does NOT belong to the same class/group as the others.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 286.

GIVEN

• Numbers: 132, 198, 264, 286

SOLUTION

• 132 = 66 × 2, 198 = 66 × 3, 264 = 66 × 4, so these three are multiples of 66 (that is, of both 6 and 11).

• 286 = 11 × 26 is a multiple of 11 but 286 ÷ 6 is not a whole number (286 ÷ 66 = 4.33...). So 286 is the odd one out.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

• Test divisibility by 6 (even and digit sum divisible by 3): 132 (sum 6), 198 (sum 18), 264 (sum 12) pass; 286 (sum 16) fails.

NOTE

• Option 1 (132), Option 2 (198) and Option 3 (264) are wrong: each is a multiple of 66, so they form the group.

question:
Charlotte is the mother of Emily, Emily is the sister of Jack, and Jack is the father of Oliver.

 

What is Charlotte’s relationship to Oliver?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Grandmother.

GIVEN

• Charlotte is the mother of Emily. Emily is the sister of Jack. Jack is the father of Oliver.

SOLUTION

• Emily and Jack are siblings, so Charlotte, who is the mother of Emily, is also the mother of Jack.

• Jack is the father of Oliver, so Charlotte is the mother of Oliver's father, which makes her Oliver's grandmother (paternal grandmother).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Mother of the father = paternal grandmother.

NOTE

• Option 2 (Mother) is wrong: Oliver's mother is not named, and Charlotte is Jack's mother. Option 3 (Aunt) is wrong: an aunt would be a sister of one of Oliver's parents; Charlotte is a generation higher. Option 4 (Sister) is wrong: Charlotte is two generations older than Oliver.

question:
Each of these questions is based on the following information:

 

Which of the following shows the relation that C is the granddaughter of E?

 

G % H means G is the son of H.

G @ H means G is the sister of H.

G $ H means G is the father of H.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. C @ B % F % E.

GIVEN

• % = son of; @ = sister of; $ = father of. C must be the granddaughter of E.

SOLUTION

• Option 1: C @ B means C is the sister of B (so C is female). B % F means B is the son of F. F % E means F is the son of E. So E is the father of F and the grandfather of B and C, and C is the granddaughter of E ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• A granddaughter is two generations below, and female: look for a chain with two "child-of" steps and a female first person (sister of).

NOTE

• Option 2 (C % B $ F $ E) is wrong: C is the son of B (male), and B is the father of F and F is the father of E, which puts C two generations above E, not below. Option 3 (C @ B $ F $ E) is wrong: C is the sister of B, B is the father of F, and F is the father of E, which places C in a generation above E. Option 4 (C @ B @ F % E) is wrong: C is the sister of B, B is the sister of F and F is the son of E, so C is the daughter of E, not the granddaughter.

question: If 3*5=23 and 4*6=34, then find 5*7.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 47.

GIVEN

• 3 * 5 = 23 and 4 * 6 = 34. Find 5 * 7.

SOLUTION

• Test the rule a * b = (a × b) + (a + b): 3 × 5 + (3 + 5) = 15 + 8 = 23 ✓, and 4 × 6 + (4 + 6) = 24 + 10 = 34 ✓.

• 5 * 7 = 5 × 7 + (5 + 7) = 35 + 12 = 47

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• a * b = ab + a + b = (a + 1)(b + 1) − 1. Check: (3 + 1)(5 + 1) − 1 = 23; (4 + 1)(6 + 1) − 1 = 34; (5 + 1)(7 + 1) − 1 = 47.

NOTE

• Option 1 (44), Option 2 (46) and Option 4 (48) are wrong: they do not match 5 × 7 + 5 + 7 = 47, which is the value given by the rule that fits both examples.

question: In which language was the book titled "Mainaahantar Padya" by Surendra Mohan Das selected for the Bal Sahitya Puraskar 2025 award?

question: Who was appointed as the Vice Chief of the Army Staff in April 2026?
solution_text:

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

EXPLANATION

question: What is the correct scientific explanation for the occurrence of solar and lunar eclipses based on the alignment of celestial bodies?

• Total solar eclipse: the Moon fully covers the Sun (the corona is seen). Annular solar eclipse: a "ring of fire" is seen when the Moon is farther away. A solar eclipse cannot be seen safely with the naked eye, while a lunar eclipse can be.

question: Which movement of the Earth is responsible for the occurrence of one complete year and influences seasonal cycles globally?

• Perihelion (the Earth nearest the Sun) is about 3 January and aphelion (farthest) about 4 July. A leap year has 366 days because of the extra ¼ day each year (accumulating to one day every four years).

• Pyruvate then goes to the mitochondria (aerobic respiration, forming CO₂ and water) or is changed in the cytoplasm to lactic acid (in muscles) or ethanol (in yeast) without oxygen. Mitochondria are called the "powerhouse of the cell".

question: Find the least number that must be added to 12,567 to make it divisible by 119.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 47.

GIVEN

• Number = 12,567. Divisor = 119.

SOLUTION

• Divide 12,567 by 119: 119 × 105 = 12,495, and 12,567 − 12,495 = 72. The remainder is 72.

• Number to be added = divisor − remainder = 119 − 72 = 47

• Check: 12,567 + 47 = 12,614 = 119 × 106 ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• To make a number divisible by d by adding, the least number to add = d − remainder.

NOTE

• Option 1 (28) is wrong: 12,567 + 28 = 12,595 = 119 × 105 + 100, which leaves a remainder of 100. Option 3 (72) is wrong: it is the remainder itself; 12,567 + 72 = 12,639 = 119 × 106 + 25, which is not divisible. Option 4 (91) is wrong: 12,658 = 119 × 106 + 44, which is not divisible.

question: What is the unit digit in (348)¹²⁴ × (244)¹²⁵?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 4.

GIVEN

• Expression: (348)¹²⁴ × (244)¹²⁵. Only the unit digits (8 and 4) matter.

SOLUTION

• Unit digit of 8ⁿ repeats in a cycle of 4: 8, 4, 2, 6. The power is 124 = 4 × 31, so the remainder is 0 and the unit digit of 8¹²⁴ is the 4th term, which is 6.

• Unit digit of 4ⁿ repeats in a cycle of 2: 4, 6. The power 125 is odd, so the unit digit of 4¹²⁵ is 4.

• Product of unit digits: 6 × 4 = 24, so the unit digit is 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Powers of 4: odd power gives 4 and even power gives 6. Powers of 8: use the remainder of the power divided by 4 (0 means the 4th term, 6).

NOTE

• Option 2 (2), Option 3 (8) and Option 4 (1) are wrong: they do not result from 6 × 4 = 24, whose unit digit is 4.

question: The ratio of the incomes of A and B is 3 : 4 and the ratio of their expenditures is 2 : 3. If each saves ₹ 3,000, what is the income of A?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ₹ 9000.

GIVEN

• Income of A : B = 3 : 4. Expenditure of A : B = 2 : 3. Each saves ₹3,000.

SOLUTION

• Let the incomes be 3x and 4x, and the expenditures be 2y and 3y.

• Savings: 3x − 2y = 3,000 … (1) and 4x − 3y = 3,000 … (2)

• Multiply (1) by 3 and (2) by 2: 9x − 6y = 9,000 and 8x − 6y = 6,000. Subtract: x = 3,000.

• Income of A = 3x = 3 × 3,000 = ₹9,000 (and income of B = ₹12,000)

• Check: expenditure of A = 9,000 − 3,000 = 6,000 and of B = 12,000 − 3,000 = 9,000, so the ratio is 6,000 : 9,000 = 2 : 3 ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Income − expenditure = saving. Use the ratios to set up two equations and eliminate the expenditure variable.

NOTE

• Option 1 (₹10,000) is wrong: expenditure of A would be 7,000 and of B (income 13,333) would be 10,333, which does not give 2 : 3. Option 3 (₹6,000) is wrong: expenditure of A would be 3,000 and of B (income 8,000) 5,000, giving 3 : 5. Option 4 (₹7,000) is wrong: expenditure of A would be 4,000 and of B (income 9,333) 6,333, which is not in the ratio 2 : 3.

question: If x varies inversely as y and x = 2 when y = 6, then the value of y when x = 3 is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 4.

GIVEN

• x varies inversely as y, so x × y = constant (k). x = 2 when y = 6.

SOLUTION

• k = 2 × 6 = 12

• When x = 3: 3 × y = 12, so y = 4

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Inverse variation: x₁y₁ = x₂y₂, so 2 × 6 = 3 × y₂ and y₂ = 4.

NOTE

• Option 1 (3), Option 2 (5) and Option 4 (6) are wrong: for them x × y would be 9, 15 and 18, not 12.

question: A varies inversely with the product of B and C. When B = 9 and C = 5, then A = 12. When B = 15 and C = 4, then the value of A is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 9.

GIVEN

• A varies inversely with B × C, so A × B × C = constant (k). B = 9, C = 5, A = 12.

SOLUTION

• k = 12 × 9 × 5 = 540

• When B = 15 and C = 4: A × 15 × 4 = 540, so A × 60 = 540 and A = 9

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• A₁B₁C₁ = A₂B₂C₂ → 12 × 45 = A₂ × 60 → A₂ = 540 ÷ 60 = 9.

NOTE

• Option 1 (8), Option 2 (4) and Option 3 (5) are wrong: for them A × B × C would be 480, 240 and 300, which are not equal to 540.

question: Simplify using BODMAS : [18 ÷ 6 + (4 - 3)] × 5 - 2
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 18.

GIVEN

• Expression: [18 ÷ 6 + (4 − 3)] × 5 − 2

SOLUTION

• Round bracket first: (4 − 3) = 1

• Inside the square bracket, division first: 18 ÷ 6 = 3, so the bracket becomes [3 + 1] = 4

• Multiplication: 4 × 5 = 20

• Subtraction: 20 − 2 = 18

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• BODMAS: Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction. Always solve the inner bracket first.

NOTE

• Option 1 (12), Option 2 (22) and Option 3 (6) are wrong: they come from skipping the order of operations (for example, 20 + 2 = 22 when the last step is added instead of subtracted).

• Source note: in the PDF, a page break falls between option 3 and option 4; the question has four options.

question: Simplify using BODMAS : [(18 ÷ 3) + (4 - 2)] × 2 - 5 + 6
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 17.

GIVEN

• Expression: [(18 ÷ 3) + (4 − 2)] × 2 − 5 + 6

SOLUTION

• Round brackets: (18 ÷ 3) = 6 and (4 − 2) = 2

• Square bracket: [6 + 2] = 8

• Multiplication: 8 × 2 = 16

• Then from left to right: 16 − 5 + 6 = 11 + 6 = 17

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• After the brackets and multiplication, only + and − are left; solve them from left to right.

NOTE

• Option 1 (−18), Option 3 (5) and Option 4 (27) are wrong: they do not follow from BODMAS. For example, doing 5 + 6 first (16 − 11 = 5) gives 5, which is the wrong order of + and −.

question: The average score of a batsman in 4 innings is 42. In the fifth innings he scores 58 runs. What is his average after 5 innings?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 45.2.

GIVEN

• Average in 4 innings = 42. Score in the 5th innings = 58.

SOLUTION

• Total runs in 4 innings = 4 × 42 = 168

• Total after 5 innings = 168 + 58 = 226

• New average = 226 ÷ 5 = 45.2

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• New average = old average + (new score − old average) ÷ number of innings = 42 + (58 − 42) ÷ 5 = 42 + 3.2 = 45.2.

NOTE

• Option 1 (44), Option 3 (46) and Option 4 (47) are wrong: they would mean a total of 220, 230 and 235 runs, but the actual total is 226.

question: The average weight of 8 students is 51 kg. If the teacher's weight is included, the average becomes 55 kg. What is the teacher's weight?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 87 kg.

GIVEN

• 8 students with an average of 51 kg. With the teacher (9 persons), the average = 55 kg.

SOLUTION

• Total weight of the students = 8 × 51 = 408 kg

• Total weight with the teacher = 9 × 55 = 495 kg

• Teacher's weight = 495 − 408 = 87 kg

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Teacher's weight = new average + (number of students × rise in average) = 55 + 8 × 4 = 87.

NOTE

• Option 1 (82 kg), Option 2 (84 kg) and Option 4 (90 kg) are wrong: with them the total would be 490, 492 and 498 kg, which gives an average of about 54.4, 54.7 and 55.3 kg, not 55 kg.

question: A pair of shoes is sold for Rs. 1530 after a discount of 10%. What was its marked price?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Rs. 1700.

GIVEN

• Selling price = Rs. 1530, discount = 10%.

SOLUTION

• Selling price = 90% of the marked price

• Marked price = 1530 × 100 ÷ 90 = Rs. 1700

• Check: 10% of 1700 = 170, and 1700 − 170 = 1530 ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• A 10% discount means SP = 9/10 of MP, so MP = 1530 × 10/9 = 1700.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Rs. 1600) is wrong: a 10% discount on it gives Rs. 1440. Option 2 (Rs. 1650) is wrong: it gives Rs. 1485. Option 4 (Rs. 1750) is wrong: it gives Rs. 1575.

question: A washing machine is marked at Rs. 30,000. During a festival, the seller offers 5% discount and then an additional 10% discount on the reduced price. What is the final selling price?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Rs. 25,650.

GIVEN

• Marked price = Rs. 30,000. Successive discounts: 5% and then 10%.

SOLUTION

• After the first discount: 30,000 × 95/100 = Rs. 28,500

• After the second discount: 28,500 × 90/100 = Rs. 25,650

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Net discount for successive discounts a% and b% = a + b − ab/100 = 5 + 10 − 0.5 = 14.5%. So the price = 85.5% of 30,000 = 25,650.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Rs. 25,500) is wrong: it comes from adding the discounts (15%), but successive discounts are applied one after the other, so the net discount is 14.5%. Option 3 (Rs. 25,750) and Option 4 (Rs. 25,900) are wrong: they would be net discounts of about 14.17% and 13.67%.

question: A shopkeeper sells two calculators for Rs. 1200 each. On one he gains 20% and on the other he loses 20%. What is his overall gain or loss?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Rs. 100 loss.

GIVEN

• Selling price of each calculator = Rs. 1200. Gain of 20% on one and loss of 20% on the other.

SOLUTION

• Calculator with 20% gain: CP = 1200 × 100 ÷ 120 = Rs. 1000

• Calculator with 20% loss: CP = 1200 × 100 ÷ 80 = Rs. 1500

• Total CP = 1000 + 1500 = Rs. 2500. Total SP = 1200 + 1200 = Rs. 2400.

• Net result = 2500 − 2400 = Rs. 100 loss

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• When two articles are sold at the same price, one at a gain of x% and one at a loss of x%, there is always a loss of (x²/100)%. Here the loss % = 20²/100 = 4% of the total CP: 4% of 2500 = Rs. 100.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Rs. 80 gain) and Option 3 (Rs. 120 gain) are wrong: equal percentage gain and loss at the same selling price always give a loss, never a gain. Option 4 (Rs. 120 loss) is wrong: the loss is Rs. 100, because the total cost is Rs. 2,500 and the total selling price is Rs. 2,400.

question: At what rate percent per annum will Rs. 2400 amount to Rs. 3120 in 5 years at simple interest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 6%.

GIVEN

• Principal = Rs. 2400, amount = Rs. 3120, time = 5 years.

SOLUTION

• Simple interest = 3120 − 2400 = Rs. 720

• Rate = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T) = (720 × 100) ÷ (2400 × 5) = 72000 ÷ 12000 = 6% per annum

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Interest per year = 720 ÷ 5 = 144. Rate = 144 ÷ 2400 × 100 = 6%.

NOTE

• Option 1 (5%) is wrong: the interest would be Rs. 600 in 5 years. Option 3 (7%) is wrong: the interest would be Rs. 840. Option 4 (8%) is wrong: the interest would be Rs. 960.

question: A number is multiplied by itself and then 175 is added to the result. If the final value is 800, what is the number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 25.

GIVEN

• Let the number be n. n × n + 175 = 800.

SOLUTION

• n² = 800 − 175 = 625

• n = √625 = 25

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Subtract 175 from 800 to get 625, which is a well-known square (25²).

NOTE

• Option 1 (15) is wrong: 15² + 175 = 400. Option 2 (20) is wrong: 20² + 175 = 575. Option 4 (30) is wrong: 30² + 175 = 1075.

question: A runner completes one round of a 400 m track in 80 seconds. What is his speed in m/s?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 5 m/s.

GIVEN

• Distance = 400 m, time = 80 seconds.

SOLUTION

• Speed = distance ÷ time = 400 ÷ 80 = 5 m/s

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Speed = distance ÷ time. Cancel zeros: 40 ÷ 8 = 5.

NOTE

• Option 1 (4 m/s) is wrong: it would cover only 320 m in 80 seconds. Option 3 (6 m/s) is wrong: it would cover 480 m. Option 4 (8 m/s) is wrong: it would cover 640 m.

question: A can complete a project in 10 days. How many days will A take to complete 60% of the project?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 6 days.

GIVEN

• A completes the whole project in 10 days.

SOLUTION

• Work and time are directly proportional for the same worker.

• Time for 60% of the project = 60% of 10 days = 0.6 × 10 = 6 days

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• A does 10% of the project per day, so 60% takes 6 days.

NOTE

• Option 1 (4 days) is wrong: A completes only 40% in 4 days. Option 2 (5 days) is wrong: A completes 50% in 5 days. Option 4 (7 days) is wrong: A completes 70% in 7 days.

question: A circular field has radius 21 m. What is the cost of fencing it at ₹4/m? (Use π = 22/7)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ₹528.

GIVEN

• Radius r = 21 m, rate = ₹4 per metre, π = 22/7.

SOLUTION

• Length of the fence = circumference = 2πr = 2 × 22/7 × 21 = 132 m

• Cost = 132 × 4 = ₹528

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Circumference = 2 × 22/7 × 21 = 2 × 22 × 3 = 132 (21 and 7 cancel).

NOTE

• Option 1 (₹484) is wrong: it would pay for a fence of 121 m. Option 3 (₹544) is wrong: it would pay for 136 m. Option 4 (₹572) is wrong: it would pay for 143 m. The circumference is 132 m.

question: The length, breadth and height of a rectangular parallelepiped are 8 cm, 5 cm and 3 cm respectively. Its volume is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 120 cm³.

GIVEN

• Length = 8 cm, breadth = 5 cm, height = 3 cm.

SOLUTION

• Volume of a cuboid = length × breadth × height = 8 × 5 × 3 = 120 cm³

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Multiply the three numbers: 8 × 5 = 40 and 40 × 3 = 120.

NOTE

• Option 2 (126 cm³), Option 3 (128 cm³) and Option 4 (132 cm³) are wrong: none equals 8 × 5 × 3. (The sum of the areas of the faces is a different quantity: the total surface area is 2(40 + 15 + 24) = 158 cm².)

question: The radius and height of a right circular cone are 7 cm and 15 cm respectively. Using π = 22/7, what is the volume of the cone?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 770 cm³.

GIVEN

• Radius r = 7 cm, height h = 15 cm, π = 22/7.

SOLUTION

• Volume of a cone = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3) × (22/7) × 7 × 7 × 15

• = (1/3) × 22 × 7 × 15 = 22 × 7 × 5 = 770 cm³

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Cancel 15 with the 3 in the denominator (15 ÷ 3 = 5), and 7 with the denominator 7: 22 × 7 × 5 = 770.

NOTE

• Option 1 (660 cm³), Option 3 (880 cm³) and Option 4 (990 cm³) are wrong: they do not equal (1/3)πr²h = 770. (Forgetting the factor 1/3 gives 2310 cm³, which is the volume of a cylinder of the same size, and is not an option.)

question: For a closed right circular cylinder, the difference between its total surface area and curved surface area is 308 cm². If π = 22/7 and the height is 8 cm more than the radius, what is the volume of the cylinder?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 2310 cm³.

GIVEN

• Total surface area − curved surface area = 308 cm². Height h = r + 8. π = 22/7.

SOLUTION

• Total surface area = 2πr(r + h) and curved surface area = 2πrh, so the difference = 2πr² (the area of the two circular ends).

• 2πr² = 308 → 2 × 22/7 × r² = 308 → r² = 308 × 7 ÷ 44 = 49 → r = 7 cm

• h = 7 + 8 = 15 cm

• Volume = πr²h = 22/7 × 49 × 15 = 22 × 7 × 15 = 2310 cm³

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• TSA − CSA = 2πr² = 308 gives πr² = 154 (the base area). Then V = 154 × 15 = 2310.

NOTE

• Option 1 (2156 cm³), Option 3 (2464 cm³) and Option 4 (2640 cm³) are wrong: with the base area of 154 cm², they would need heights of 14, 16 and about 17.14 cm, but h = 7 + 8 = 15 cm.

question: A hollow spherical shell has external radius 4 cm and internal radius 3 cm. What is the volume of the metal used?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (148/3)π cm³.

GIVEN

• External radius R = 4 cm, internal radius r = 3 cm.

SOLUTION

• Volume of metal = volume of the outer sphere − volume of the inner sphere = (4/3)π(R³ − r³)

• R³ = 64 and r³ = 27, so R³ − r³ = 37

• Volume = (4/3) × π × 37 = (148/3)π cm³

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Use the formula V = (4/3)π(R³ − r³) directly; remember the cubes 3³ = 27 and 4³ = 64.

NOTE

• Option 2 (36π cm³) is wrong: it would need (4/3)(R³ − r³) = 36, so R³ − r³ = 27, which ignores the outer sphere. Option 3 (76π cm³) and Option 4 (84π cm³) are wrong: they do not equal (4/3) × 37 = 49.33.

question: Which of the following fractions has a terminating decimal expansion?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 11/40.

GIVEN

• Fractions: 11/40, 7/24, 13/45 and 17/60.

SOLUTION

• A fraction in its lowest terms has a terminating decimal expansion only if the prime factors of its denominator are 2 and/or 5.

• 40 = 2³ × 5 → only 2 and 5, so 11/40 = 0.275 terminates.

• 24 = 2³ × 3 → has the factor 3. 45 = 3² × 5 → has the factor 3. 60 = 2² × 3 × 5 → has the factor 3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Check the denominator: if it contains any prime other than 2 or 5 (here 3), the decimal does not terminate.

NOTE

• Option 2 (7/24 = 0.291666...), Option 3 (13/45 = 0.28888...) and Option 4 (17/60 = 0.28333...) are wrong: each denominator has the prime factor 3, so the decimals are non-terminating (recurring).

question: A runner completes 5/6 of a marathon in 3.5 hours. If they maintain the same speed, how many minutes will it take them to finish the remaining portion of the race?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 42 minutes.

GIVEN

• 5/6 of the marathon takes 3.5 hours. The speed stays the same.

SOLUTION

• Remaining portion = 1 − 5/6 = 1/6 of the marathon.

• 5/6 of the race takes 3.5 hours = 210 minutes, so 1/6 of the race takes 210 ÷ 5 = 42 minutes

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• 5 parts take 210 minutes, so 1 part takes 210 ÷ 5 = 42 minutes; the remaining part is 1 part.

NOTE

• Option 1 (40 minutes), Option 3 (30 minutes) and Option 4 (28 minutes) are wrong: at a speed of 5 parts in 210 minutes, 1 part needs exactly 42 minutes, not 40, 30 or 28.

question: A 12 cm × 8 cm rectangle has a 4 cm × 2 cm rectangle cut out from one corner. What is the perimeter of the resulting shape?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 40 cm.

GIVEN

• Rectangle: 12 cm × 8 cm. A 4 cm × 2 cm rectangle is cut from one corner.

SOLUTION

• Perimeter of the original rectangle = 2 × (12 + 8) = 40 cm.

• Cutting a rectangle out of a corner removes two outer sides (4 cm and 2 cm) and adds two new sides of the same lengths (4 cm and 2 cm) inside, so the perimeter does not change.

• Perimeter of the resulting shape = 40 cm

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• A corner cut-out never changes the perimeter of the figure; only the area changes.

NOTE

• Option 2 (30 cm) and Option 4 (20 cm) are wrong: they are smaller than the perimeter of the original rectangle, but the perimeter stays the same. Option 3 (50 cm) is wrong: it would need an extra 10 cm of boundary, which a corner cut does not add.

question: A 20 cm × 15 cm rectangle has a 5 cm × 5 cm square cut out from one corner. Find the perimeter of the resulting figure.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 70 cm.

GIVEN

• Rectangle: 20 cm × 15 cm. A 5 cm × 5 cm square is cut from one corner.

SOLUTION

• Perimeter of the original rectangle = 2 × (20 + 15) = 70 cm.

• The corner cut removes 5 cm + 5 cm of outer boundary and adds 5 cm + 5 cm of new boundary, so the perimeter is unchanged.

• Perimeter of the resulting figure = 70 cm

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Corner cut-outs do not change the perimeter, so just find 2(l + b) = 2(20 + 15) = 70.

NOTE

• Option 1 (40 cm), Option 2 (60 cm) and Option 4 (50 cm) are wrong: they are less than the perimeter of the original rectangle, but a corner cut keeps the perimeter at 70 cm.

question:

question: Choose the antonym of Hostile.

question: Choose the antonym of Benevolent.
solution_text:

question:
In the following question, four sentences from a paragraph are provided. The sentences are jumbled and labeled A, B, C and D. Rearrange these sentences into the correct sequence to form a logically and grammatically coherent paragraph. From the given alternatives, select the option that represents the correct sequence.

 

A. Hence, consumption of excessive salt in daily food, packaged and canned foods need to be avoided.

B. Use of excess salt is linked with hypertension.

C. If you are in the habit of adding table salt to your food you are consuming excess salt.

D. All packaged and canned food items contain a very high level of sodium because of the presence of salt that is used as a preservative.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. DCBA.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• D ("All packaged and canned food items contain a very high level of sodium…") states the starting fact about hidden salt in packaged food.

 

• C ("If you are in the habit of adding table salt…") adds a second source of salt, so it follows D.

 

• B ("Use of excess salt is linked with hypertension.") gives the harmful result of the excess salt from D and C.

 

• A begins with "Hence", so it is the conclusion and comes last.

◦ Correct order: D – C – B – A

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (CBAD) is wrong, because A ("Hence…") would come before D, although A depends on the facts in D.

 

• Option 2 (ADCB) is wrong, because it begins with the conclusion "Hence".

 

• Option 3 (CBDA) is wrong, because it starts with C and B, so the argument about salt in packaged food (D) comes only at the end, after which A ("Hence…") does not follow naturally. (The PDF shows this option as a wrong selection.)

 

NOTE

 

• Trick: sentences starting with "Hence", "Therefore", "Thus" are conclusions, and so go last.

question:
In the following question, four sentences from a paragraph are provided. The sentences are jumbled and labeled A, B, C and D. Rearrange these sentences into the correct sequence to form a logically and grammatically coherent paragraph. From the given alternatives, select the option that represents the correct sequence.

 

A. These are Dam (blood), Balgham (phlegm), Safra (yellow bile) and Sanda (black bile).

B. The Unani medicines are given to the person suffering from a disease to promote an equilibrium of these elements in the body.

C. Unani system of medicine is also the natural way of treatment with the help of herbal medicines.

D. According to this system, the health of a person depends on the balance of four elements in the body.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. CDAB.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• C introduces the topic (the Unani system of medicine), so it comes first.

 

• D ("According to this system…") refers to the system named in C and mentions "four elements".

 

• A ("These are Dam, Balgham, Safra and Sanda") names the four elements, so it follows D.

 

• B ("these elements") closes the paragraph with the use of the medicines to restore the balance.

◦ Correct order: C – D – A – B

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (ADCB) is wrong, because A ("These are…") has nothing to refer to at the start.

 

• Option 2 (BDCA) is wrong, because B ("these elements") comes before the elements are mentioned.

 

• Option 4 (CADB) is wrong, because A ("These are…") comes before D introduces the "four elements".

 

NOTE

 

• Trick: pronoun starters ("These", "It", "According to this") need an earlier noun to refer to, so they cannot be first.
